subject: Horizon AI PoC — orchestration, SDK/auth, and prompt governance next steps

Subject: Horizon AI PoC kickoff — recap + decisions needed

Elena / Tim — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the minimal decisions we need to lock so the PoC (2-week sprint) can start on Apr 12. I pulled the notes into bullets so it's actionable.

Key customer goals
- Support tickets: reduce first-response time by surfacing KB answers and suggested replies (embeddings + reranker).
- Sensitive PII filters at inference time; strict retention policy (30 days).
- Production-grade latency target: 95th percentile < 160ms for short queries.

Technical constraints you mentioned
- Primary auth: Okta (OIDC) for employee users; callouts to external vendor APIs will require scoped tokens.
- Production network: VPC peering preferred; strict outbound egress controls.
- Procurement: SOC 2 + network diagrams required for legal.

Immediate asks / decisions (please confirm by EOD Wed 4/7)
1) Authorize Redwood to use API-key auth for initial integration/testing and agree to mTLS+OIDC for production.
2) Confirm which KB will be the first index: Support KB (support.horizonai.com) or Docs (docs.horizonai.com).
3) Agree on redacted sample dataset for embedding tuning (we need ~5k sample queries + canonical answers).

Attachments: Horizon_PoC_SOW.pdf (draft SOW), redwood_sdk_setup_guide.pdf (dev quickstart), prompt_templates_v0.3.md (initial templates).

Next steps (internal / external owners)
- Aditya: Draft final SOW and schedule engineer sync (by 4/8).
- Marissa: Confirm procurement path & provide contact at Horizon legal (by 4/7).
- Laura: Prepare security checklist and SOC2 pointer for Horizon (by 4/9).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Thanks Aditya — good summary. Quick clarifications from our side: we can approve the API-key flow for dev/testing but our security team will insist on OIDC for any staging/production endpoints (Okta-backed). For production-facing inference you'll need to sit behind our VPC with egress rules — our infra team will share details.

On the KB selection: start with Support KB first (support.horizonai.com). We'll provide a read-only S3 export for the PoC.

About the sample dataset: we can produce a redacted set of ~3k queries initially and iterate — can you confirm the CSV schema you need (query, user_metadata, ground_truth_reply)? Also, how are you planning to do reranking — first-pass retriever with dense embeddings + lightweight lexical reranker, or the reverse?

Procurement: I looped in Tim (ops) — he will be our procurement lead. He'll follow up on SOC2 and network diagrams; can you send the security binder you mentioned?

On prompt safety: we have a couple of concerns around prompt injection since some customer inputs include system-like directives. Please include your recommended mitigations for prompt injection in the PoC deliverables.

Thanks — great questions. Short answers up front, then proposed PoC architecture and governance plan below.

Answers
- CSV schema: please send a CSV with columns: query, context_uri, user_role (agent/end-user), ground_truth_reply, created_at (ISO). 3k rows is fine to start.
- Reranker plan: recommend dense embeddings retriever (fast ANN) + light lexical reranker for precision; for support workloads we'll tune a small learned reranker in week 2 of the PoC and compare.
- Security binder: attaching our standard security binder and the SDK quickstart. (attachments: redwood_sdk_setup_guide.pdf, prompt_templates_v0.3.md)

Proposed PoC architecture (high level)- Ingestion: we ingest support KB dump into a vector store (Milvus by default for PoC).
- Embeddings: customer data flows to a dedicated embedding pipeline; keys scoped and rotated. For dev we use customer-provided API-key; for prod we will use mTLS + OIDC client assertion for Redwood to call your index endpoints.
- Serving: inference calls from your app -> Redwood SDK (browser / server) -> Redwood routing layer. Routing policy: dev traffic to hosted test model, staging to dedicated reserved model (quantized), prod to VPC-deployed instance inside Horizon network.
- Structured output & tool calling: recommend the following approach for KB lookups — model returns structured JSON with a hit id and confidence, then a server-side deterministic tool validates hit and sources before sending to user. We'll enable function-calling hooks for retrieval augmentation.

Prompt governance (short plan)
- Prompt templates: store templated system + user prompts in a git-backed repo with semver tags. Each template has a schema (placeholders, pre/post-processing).
- Versioning: adopt semantic versioning for prompt templates (major = behavior changes, minor = new slots, patch = wording). All changes require a small eval against regression prompts.
- Injection mitigations: canonicalize user input, strip high-risk tokens, and apply an allowlist for tool-calling functions. In addition we will add sentinel markers in the system prompt (e.g., "<USER_INPUT_START>") and run a lightweight static analyzer to flag suspicious directives prior to sending to the model.
- Red teaming: we'll schedule two red-team passes during PoC: exploratory (week 1) and adversarial (week 2) focusing on prompt injection and hallucination triggers. We’ll provide a short report after each pass.

Next actions I will take this week
- Deliver final SOW (Aditya) — 4/8
- Engineer sync to walk infra team through VPC peering / egress (Ben) — propose 4/9
- Provide security binder and SOC2 pointer (Laura) — 4/9
- Upload initial prompt templates repo and example evals (Marissa) — 4/8

Happy to discuss further on a call — propose Wed 4/7 10am PT for an engineering sync.

Aditya / team — good thread. Quick summary and explicit assignments so procurement/security have a single list.

Action items (owner / deliverable / due)
- Aditya: Finalized SOW reflecting OIDC for prod + VPC peering details; provide statement of work for procurement (due 2027-04-08).
- Ben: Engineer sync with Horizon infra to confirm subnet ranges, peering steps, and egress rules; share a short runbook after call (due 2027-04-09).
- Marissa: Collect procurement contacts and lead negotiations on commercial terms; confirm PoC billing profile (credit-based vs usage) (due 2027-04-07).
- Laura: Security binder + SOC2 link + network diagram template for Horizon to fill; include redwood's prompt governance summary (due 2027-04-09).
- Elena / Tim (Horizon): Provide read-only S3 export of Support KB, and a redacted CSV sample (3k rows) using the CSV schema above (due 2027-04-08).

Notes on prompt governance to include in binder
- We'll include a prompt-template registry example (git + pull-request gating) and an eval harness that runs regression checks on changed templates.
- For the PoC scope: we will only enable tool-calling for KB retrieval confirmations; no external tool execution until adversarial tests pass.
- Reranker baseline: dense retriever + lexical reranker; learn-to-rank candidate will be an optional metric-driven experiment in week 2.

I will package the security binder and the minimal prompt-governance one-pager and upload to the shared Drive link (see related_links). Aditya — please confirm the Wed 4/7 10am PT time and I'll send calendar invites to all.
